_note: Built-in anti-spike quests and cheap home meals. The server falls back to these when the AI is unavailable, and the web app's demo mode uses them too. Meal macros and costs are per serving (US grocery prices, 2026).

quests.title: Take a 10-minute walk within 30 minutes of eating
quests.why: Working muscles pull sugar out of your blood on their own, so the peak comes out lower.

quests.title: Do 2 minutes of squats or stair climbing after a meal
quests.why: Even a few minutes of movement right after eating trims the spike.

quests.title: Do 3 sets of calf raises while you sit or stand after eating
quests.why: Calf muscles burn glucose steadily, and you can do this at a desk or on the couch.

quests.title: Dance to 3 songs after a meal
quests.why: About 10 minutes of fun movement during the rise, when it helps most.

quests.title: Spend 15 minutes on your feet after dinner (dishes, tidying, a stroll)
quests.why: Evening meals often spike higher because you sit afterward. Standing and moving helps.

quests.title: Eat the vegetables first, then protein, then the starch
quests.why: In small studies, eating carbs last lowered the spike by about a third.

quests.title: Start one meal with a side salad or raw veggies
quests.why: Fiber eaten first slows how fast the rest of the meal turns into sugar.

quests.title: Pair your next carb snack with protein (cheese, nuts, peanut butter or yogurt)
quests.why: Protein and fat slow digestion, so the same carbs make a smaller, later peak.

quests.title: Add beans, lentils or chickpeas to one meal
quests.why: Beans add fiber and protein for cents, and both flatten the curve.

quests.title: Use a vinegar dressing on a side salad with a starchy meal
quests.why: A tablespoon of vinegar with a meal slightly lowers the rise in several small trials.

quests.title: Swap white bread, rice or pasta for a whole-grain version at one meal
quests.why: Whole grains have more fiber, which slows the sugar rush.

quests.title: Drink water or unsweetened tea instead of soda or juice at one meal
quests.why: Sugary drinks are absorbed fastest of all foods and stack on top of the meal's spike.

quests.title: Choose whole fruit instead of juice today
quests.why: The fiber in whole fruit keeps its sugar from hitting all at once.

quests.title: Use rice, pasta or potatoes cooked earlier and cooled in the fridge
quests.why: Cooling turns some starch into resistant starch, which raises blood sugar less, even reheated.

quests.title: Fill half your plate with vegetables at one meal
quests.why: Keep eating until you're full; the veggies just take room from the fastest carbs.

quests.title: Drink a glass of water with each meal today
quests.why: Being well hydrated helps your kidneys clear extra sugar.

quests.title: Get to bed 30 minutes earlier tonight
quests.why: After a short night, the same breakfast can spike noticeably higher.

quests.title: Take a 5-minute breathing or stretch break
quests.why: Stress hormones like cortisol push blood sugar up even without food.

quests.title: Plan a protein-rich breakfast for tomorrow
quests.why: A breakfast with protein sets up steadier glucose for the rest of the day.

quests.title: Wash and chop veggies or cook a pot of beans for the week
quests.why: Ready-to-go fiber makes the steady choice the easy one later.

quests.title: Cook one meal at home from the Meals tab
quests.why: Home meals give you control over the carbs, fiber and cost.

quests.title: Finish dinner at least 2 hours before bed
quests.why: Your body handles sugar less well late at night, so earlier dinners spike less.

quests.title: Eat a full breakfast or lunch with protein instead of grazing on snacks
quests.why: Steady meals avoid the up-and-down of sugary snacking.

meals.name: Black bean and egg breakfast tacos
steps: Scramble the eggs with the spinach in a pan.
Warm the beans and tortillas.
Fill the tortillas and top with salsa.
meals.why: Eggs and beans bring protein and fiber, and corn tortillas are a slower carb than white bread.

meals.name: Peanut butter overnight oats
steps: Stir everything together in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Eat cold or microwave 1 minute.
meals.why: Rolled oats with chia and peanut butter digest slowly, unlike instant flavored packets.

meals.name: Greek yogurt bowl with berries and walnuts
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with berries, walnuts and cinnamon.
meals.why: High protein, modest carbs, and frozen berries cost less than fresh.

meals.name: Veggie scramble with whole-wheat toast
ingredients: 1/2 bell pepper or a handful of spinach
steps: Saute the vegetables in the oil for 2 minutes.
Add the eggs and scramble.
Serve with the toast.
meals.why: Protein first thing in the morning keeps the whole day steadier.

meals.name: One-pot lentil soup
steps: Saute the chopped onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add lentils, tomatoes, water and spices.
Simmer 25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
meals.why: Lentils are one of the cheapest sources of fiber and protein, and they rise slowly.

meals.name: Tuna and white bean salad
steps: Mix the tuna, beans and cucumber.
Dress with oil, lemon, salt and pepper.
meals.why: No cooking, lots of protein, and beans instead of bread.

meals.name: Chicken and veggie stir-fry with brown rice
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil.
Add the frozen vegetables and garlic, cook 5 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce and serve over the rice.
meals.why: Lots of vegetables and a half cup of rice instead of a full plate of it.

meals.name: Chickpea and spinach curry
steps: Saute the onion with the curry powder.
Add chickpeas and tomatoes, simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in spinach until wilted; serve with the rice.
meals.why: Chickpeas bring so much fiber that the rice hits more gently.

meals.name: Sheet-pan chicken, broccoli and sweet potato
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F.
Toss everything with the oil and spices on a sheet pan.
Roast 25 minutes.
meals.why: Sweet potato with skin plus broccoli gives a slower, smaller rise than fries or white potatoes.

meals.name: Turkey and bean chili
steps: Brown the turkey with the chopped onion.
Add beans, tomatoes and spices.
Simmer 20 minutes. Freezes well.
meals.why: A big batch for the week, with beans doing the work of the carbs.

meals.name: Apple slices with peanut butter
steps: Slice the apple.
Dip in the peanut butter.
meals.why: Whole fruit with fat and protein instead of chips or candy.

meals.name: Hummus, veggie sticks and a hard-boiled egg
steps: Cut the vegetables into sticks.
Serve with hummus and the egg.
meals.why: Crunchy, filling and very low in fast carbs.

meals.name: Black bean quesadilla with a side salad
steps: Spread beans and cheese on half the tortilla and fold.
Cook in a dry pan 2 minutes per side.
Serve with salsa and the salad.
meals.why: Beans and cheese balance the tortilla, and the salad adds more fiber.

meals.name: Tofu and veggie stir-fry with peanut sauce
steps: Pan-fry the tofu until golden.
Add the vegetables and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter, soy sauce and lime thinned with water.
meals.why: Plant protein, lots of vegetables, and no rice needed.

meals.name: Canned salmon patties with green beans
steps: Mix the salmon, egg and oats; shape 4 patties.
Pan-fry 3 minutes per side.
Steam the green beans and serve with lemon.
meals.why: Canned salmon is a cheap source of protein and healthy fat.

meals.name: Whole-wheat pasta with chickpeas and marinara
steps: Boil the pasta.
Warm the marinara with the chickpeas and spinach.
Toss together.
meals.why: Keeps the pasta night, with twice the fiber of regular spaghetti.

meals.name: Cottage cheese with tomato and cucumber
steps: Chop the vegetables.
Mix into the cottage cheese and season.
meals.why: A savory, high-protein snack with almost no sugar rise.

meals.name: Crunchy roasted chickpeas
steps: Rinse and pat the chickpeas dry.
Toss with oil and spices.
Roast at 400 F for 25 minutes.
meals.why: A cheap, crunchy swap for chips.

meals.name: Bean and veggie burrito bowl
steps: Warm the rice and beans.
Top with cabbage, salsa and avocado.
meals.why: Half the rice of a takeout bowl, and the beans and cabbage slow the rest.

meals.name: Egg and veggie fried rice
steps: Scramble the eggs in the oil and set aside.
Fry the vegetables and cold rice 4 minutes.
Stir the eggs and soy sauce back in.
meals.why: Cold leftover rice has more resistant starch, and eggs and veggies balance it.
